title: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub says Copilot app and Copilot CLI now respect enterprise, organization, and repository content exclusion policies, so excluded files are not used as context across agentic workflows.
actionable_takeaway: Create a Context Exclusion Contract before agent runs: excluded paths, policy level, applicable tools, exception approver, and post-run public-boundary scan.

title: Enterprise-managed settings support any default model
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Enterprise administrators can set the default Copilot model for new conversations and customize defaults by enterprise team through team mappings.
actionable_takeaway: Treat default model selection as a config release: record model key, team mapping, overridable flag, rollout scope, and rollback path.

title: ChatGPT for iOS 1.2026.237 adds attachment-aware mobile queue controls
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT & Codex changelog
why_it_matters: The iOS update emphasizes queued prompts, background sending, Priority view, file/image/PDF attachment support, work-time display, and thread ID copying for Codex Remote workflows.
actionable_takeaway: Use a Mobile Attachment Queue Envelope: origin device, attachment list, public/private mark, queue status, thread ID, and Mac/Codex final evidence.

title: Healthcare plugins split organization data and public health data
author: OpenAI Help / ChatGPT Release Notes
why_it_matters: OpenAI describes healthcare plugins for EHR/claims integration and a Healthcare Public Data plugin for read-only public health information, with a clear warning not to send PHI to public sources.
actionable_takeaway: Separate public medical-information lookup from personal health-data handling; PHI, claims, and records require an organization connector and explicit approval.

title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83-2 adds custom-agent model lists and proxy egress control
author: GitHub / GitHub releases
why_it_matters: Custom agents can list several models tried in order and use a required model policy to keep changes on that list; Linux sandboxes can restrict network egress to the configured proxy.
actionable_takeaway: For every execution channel, keep an allowed-model list and proxy-egress gate; do not allow silent fallback to unapproved models or direct network paths.

title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83-3 ships a prerelease fixes batch
author: GitHub / GitHub releases
why_it_matters: The next Copilot CLI prerelease followed hours after 1.0.83-2 but only exposes a generic fixes-and-changes release body, so it is useful for cadence awareness rather than feature claims.
actionable_takeaway: Track prerelease cadence separately from stable operating guidance; require concrete release notes before turning a prerelease into a workflow rule.

title: Codex 0.153 alpha builds continue rolling after 0.152 stable
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: OpenAI published multiple 0.153 alpha builds around September 2-3, including 0.153.0-alpha.5.1 on September 3 UTC, while release bodies provide little behavioral detail.
actionable_takeaway: Keep Codex 0.153 alpha in an observation lane and validate against stable 0.152.x before accepting any workflow change.

title: Codex CLI 0.152.0 remains the stable runtime governance baseline
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: The stable release documents MCP output_token_limit, longer app-server shellCommand timeouts, credential refresh progress, package-style MCP names, and trusted backend URL handling.
actionable_takeaway: Use 0.152.0 as the current stable checklist for long commands, MCP output ceilings, credential refresh state, and backend URL trust.

title: Copilot code review can now approve pull requests
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Copilot now surfaces approval assessments in reviews and can submit approvals only when administrators explicitly enable it; assessments alone do not count toward merge requirements.
actionable_takeaway: Keep AI assessment, comments, formal approval, and required-approval rules as separate states in review governance.

title: GitHub adds expiration dates for individual user budgets
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Administrators can set individual user budget overrides to expire at the next billing cycle or on a specific date, including through the Budgets REST API expires_at field.
actionable_takeaway: Give temporary agent or model trials expiring budgets and include expires_at in every high-cost execution lane receipt.

title: Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available in GitHub Copilot
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: The model targets long-horizon autonomous coding but carries data-retention requirements by default unless eligible enterprise zero-retention access is approved and enabled.
actionable_takeaway: Before selecting a long-horizon coding model, record retention mode, zero-retention eligibility, administrator approval, and allowed surfaces.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK Python 0.22.0 hardens replay and usage accounting
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: The release redacts blocked terminal output from replayable state, rejects terminal failed/incomplete Responses, rejects ignored explicit-client options, and isolates usage across RunState checkpoints.
actionable_takeaway: Before SDK upgrades, test blocked-output replay, terminal failure handling, explicit-client rejection, and checkpoint usage isolation.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK JS 0.17.0 fails closed on ambiguous approval checkpoint replay
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: The JS SDK blocks ambiguous serialized approval replays, withholds rejected final tool output in SDK-owned replay surfaces, and clarifies that external side effects are not undone automatically.
actionable_takeaway: Define a replay-safe guardrail contract for live state, serialized checkpoints, new runs, and application-owned logs.

title: ChatGPT App Store 1.2026.237 confirms current mobile build availability
author: OpenAI / Apple App Store
why_it_matters: The public App Store listing exposes the current ChatGPT mobile build stream, which helps cross-check whether a documented iOS workflow is plausibly available as an app update.
actionable_takeaway: For mobile workflow claims, pair product changelog reading with public app-version readback, then still verify the user's device before relying on it.
